LESSON: CITIZENSHIP

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Developments and Governance
Topic 5.3: Citizenship
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Citizenship, part of Political Developments and Governance in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we promote global citizenship? 2. How can we show empathy as global citizens?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Citizenship together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Patriotism: learners promote democracy and Rule of Law as they become aware of their own responsibilities in the society when

describing the qualities and responsibilities of a global citizen.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Civic responsibility: learners become aware about responsibilities of as global citizens when developing communication messages or

posters on responsibilities of a global citizen in the world today.

Link to other subjects:

● Religious education: learners gain more knowledge about factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and

Africa.

● Creative arts: as learners practice sign singing the Eastern Africa (EAC) and African Union (AU) anthems.
